gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180 + 2×200 W kit gets its full 400 W only if the two SP200L panels are wired in series. The AC180's solar input is capped at 10 A (12–60 V). Each SP200L's short-circuit current (Isc) is 10.8 A and its open-circuit voltage (Voc) is 24.6 V. Wired in parallel, the pair therefore cannot deliver more than about 246 W, so a full charge takes at least 4.7 sun-hours instead of 2.9. In series the pair is 49.2 V Voc, which is under the 60 V limit, so all 400 W can reach the battery.
standout_why: Trek4Tech (cited) lists the AC180 only with one 200 W panel. It gives a 500 W max input with no voltage or amp limits and no wiring guidance for two panels. RuntimeMath gives a 13 A limit only for the ALLPOWERS R1500 + SP039 and says nothing about series vs parallel. Our own dealectric.com page shows AC180 + 2×200 W at 2.9 h (1,152 ÷ 400) with the station's input limits marked 'Not given', so that 2.9 h is right only with series wiring. I could not read TheOutagePlan (cited) because of an SSL certificate error, so it is unchecked. None of the pages I read set each station's amp cap against the bundled panel's current.
decides: This does not change the fastest pick on panel-to-battery ratio. That is the ALLPOWERS P1800 kits: 1,024 Wh with 600 W of panel, about 1.7 h at rated panel watts, or with 400 W, about 2.6 h. The P1800's solar input is 650 W, which is above both panel sizes. The finding sets a condition on the next-fastest kit. The BLUETTI AC180 + 2×200 W ($1,232) is about 2.9 h only in series and at least 4.7 h in parallel, which would put it behind both P1800 kits by a wide margin. The Elite 200 V2 has a 20 A input, so its 2×200 W kit (about 5.2 h) is not affected much by wiring. The page should give 'wire in series' as the instruction for the AC180 kit.

findings.value: 12–60 V DC, 10 A max, 500 W max; series or parallel allowed; Voc must not exceed 60 V
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)

findings.label: Panel electrical specs
findings.value: Voc 24.6 V, Isc 10.8 A, 200 W max
findings.note: The page does not list Vmp or Imp. The AC180 2×200 W kit image filename is 'AC180_2xSP200L', which suggests the kit uses this panel.

findings.label: Highest possible solar watts when wired in parallel
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: In parallel the two panels together give 2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A Isc, which is clipped to the 10 A input cap. Voltage stays under 24.6 V Voc, so the most power possible is 10 A × 24.6 V = 246 W, and the real figure at Vmp is lower. 1,152 Wh ÷ 246 W = 4.7 h, before losses. In series, Voc is 2 × 24.6 = 49.2 V, under the 60 V limit, and current stays at or below 10.8 A Isc. That allows up to about 400 W, so 1,152 ÷ 400 = 2.9 h. The panel's Isc is slightly above the 10 A cap, so expect a little clipping in full sun.

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.note: Two SP200L in parallel give 21.6 A Isc, close to the 20 A cap. The most power possible is 20 A × 24.6 V = 492 W, which is more than 400 W, so either wiring gives about 400 W. 2,073.6 Wh ÷ 400 W = 5.2 h. Kit price is $1,499.00. The page also claims '80% in 1.1 hours' (TurboBoost) without naming the charging source, so it is not a solar figure.

findings.label: Solar input max and kit prices (ALLPOWERS US)
findings.note: Prices and the 650 W figure come from the storecheck Shopify query. The kit URLs are …/allpowers-1800w-solar-generator-p1800-1024wh-with-400w-solar-panel and …-with-600w-solar-panel. The listed 0–80% in about 1 hour is for AC charging, not solar. At rated panel watts: 1,024 ÷ 600 = 1.7 h and 1,024 ÷ 400 = 2.6 h. Both panel sizes are under the 650 W cap.
